description: Introduce the adapter registry spine and generalize the two coupled seams around it, keeping DAD byte-identical. (a) Add src/targets.js mapping target name -> { adapterFactory, policyId, adapterId } with resolveTarget(name='dad') and isRegisteredAdapter(id); register dad -> DadAdapter with policyId 'impactgraph-discovery' and adapterId 'impactgraph' (unchanged literals). (b) Parameterize the discovery auth-cookie NAME so it is sourced from the actor descriptor, defaulting to 'dad_donor_session'. (c) Relax policy.js's adapter lock to accept any registered adapter id while keeping ALL other validation strict. (d) Parameterize discoveryPolicy()/executeDiscovery by a target, resolving the adapterFactory/adapterId/policyId from the registry; for target 'dad' the emitted policy id/adapter and digest MUST be byte-identical to today. This feature is a prerequisite for FEAT-002.
steps: Create src/targets.js (ESM). Import { DadAdapter } from './dad.js'. Export `targets` object: dad -> { adapterFactory: (run, options) => new DadAdapter(run, options), policyId: 'impactgraph-discovery', adapterId: 'impactgraph' }. (The `benchmark` entry is added in FEAT-002; FEAT-001 may register only `dad`, or register `benchmark` with a lazy dynamic import — but FEAT-001 must leave the registry and all tests green with only `dad` required.) Export resolveTarget(name = 'dad') that returns targets[name] or throws `Unknown target: <name>. Known targets: <list>.`. Export isRegisteredAdapter = id => Object.values(targets).some(t => t.adapterId === id).

Edit src/discovery-browser.js: in bootstrap(context, who) change the addCookies entry name from the literal 'dad_donor_session' to `who.cookieName ?? 'dad_donor_session'`. Change nothing else in that file.

Edit src/dad.js: in discoveryFixture(), add `cookieName: 'dad_donor_session'` to each of the two authenticated donor actor descriptors (donor-a / donor-b, the ones carrying `cookie`). Leave the guest actor untouched.

Edit src/policy.js: import { isRegisteredAdapter } from './targets.js'. In validatePolicy replace the `policy.adapter !== 'impactgraph'` condition inside the identity check with `!isRegisteredAdapter(policy.adapter)`. Leave every other validation (schemaVersion, id regex, version regex, scope, checks/evidence/scenario/digest/blocking-severities/exceptions) exactly as-is. Confirm policies/impactgraph-local.json (adapter 'impactgraph') still validates.

Edit src/discovery-runner.js: import { resolveTarget } from './targets.js'. Change `discoveryPolicy()` to `discoveryPolicy(target = 'dad')`; inside it resolve `const { policyId, adapterId } = resolveTarget(target)` and set `definition.id = policyId` and `definition.adapter = adapterId` (instead of the literals). In executeDiscovery, add a `target = 'dad'` option to the destructured params; resolve `const resolved = resolveTarget(target)`; default the `adapterFactory` param to `resolved.adapterFactory` (keep allowing an explicit adapterFactory override for tests); call `discoveryPolicy(target)`; and pass `adapter: resolved.adapterId` to Run.create instead of the literal 'impactgraph'. For target 'dad' all three (id, adapter, digest) must be byte-identical to current output.

Add test/targets.test.js (node:test): assert resolveTarget('dad') returns an object whose adapterFactory is a function and policyId==='impactgraph-discovery', adapterId==='impactgraph'; resolveTarget('nope') throws; isRegisteredAdapter('impactgraph') === true and isRegisteredAdapter('bogus') === false. Import discoveryPolicy from ../src/discovery-runner.js and assert discoveryPolicy('dad').definition.id==='impactgraph-discovery', .adapter==='impactgraph', and discoveryPolicy('dad').digest === discoveryPolicy().digest (proves DAD byte-identical).

Extend test/policy.test.js: add a test that a valid exploration policy whose adapter is a registered non-impactgraph id passes validatePolicy, while an unregistered adapter id throws. Build the valid policy by cloning discoveryPolicy('dad').definition and setting adapter to a registered id; for the negative case set adapter to 'unregistered-xyz'. Keep all existing malformed-policy cases intact (do not delete coverage).

Add a DAD cookie-name assertion: in test/adapter.test.js (or test/targets.test.js) assert that a DadAdapter discoveryFixture() authenticated actor carries cookieName 'dad_donor_session'. If exercising discoveryFixture() directly is awkward (it issues SQL), stub adapter.sql like the existing donor-verifier test does and assert the returned actors' cookieName. Do not weaken the existing adapter test.
acceptance_criteria: `npm test` passes all existing unit tests plus the new/updated ones (baseline was 101 passing).
test/targets.test.js proves discoveryPolicy('dad') emits id 'impactgraph-discovery', adapter 'impactgraph', and digest equal to discoveryPolicy() (DAD byte-identical).
policy.js accepts a registered non-impactgraph adapter and still rejects an unregistered one and all previously-rejected malformed policies.
The DAD discovery cookie name still defaults to 'dad_donor_session'.
findings: src/targets.js exports (named, ESM): `targets` (object), `resolveTarget(name = 'dad')` (returns the target entry or throws `Unknown target: <name>. Known targets: <csv>.`), and `isRegisteredAdapter = id => ...` (boolean). Registry currently holds ONLY `dad -> { adapterFactory: (run, options) => new DadAdapter(run, options), policyId: 'impactgraph-discovery', adapterId: 'impactgraph' }`. NO `benchmark` entry was registered (not even a lazy one) — FEAT-002 must add the `benchmark` entry to `targets` (a lazy dynamic import of discovery-benchmark is the suggested pattern) and add its own tests; only `dad` was needed to keep FEAT-001 green. discovery-runner.js: `discoveryPolicy(target = 'dad')` now resolves policyId/adapterId from the registry and sets definition.id/definition.adapter from them (verified byte-identical digest to discoveryPolicy() for 'dad'); the unused `DadAdapter` import was removed. `executeDiscovery` gained a `target = 'dad'` option; it calls `resolveTarget(target)`, defaults `adapterFactory` to `resolved.adapterFactory` (explicit adapterFactory override still honored for test mocks via `adapterFactory ??= resolved.adapterFactory`), calls `discoveryPolicy(target)`, and passes `adapter: resolved.adapterId` to Run.create. policy.js: imports `isRegisteredAdapter` from ./targets.js; the identity check now uses `!isRegisteredAdapter(policy.adapter)` instead of the `!== 'impactgraph'` literal — all other validation untouched; policies/impactgraph-local.json (adapter 'impactgraph') still validates. Cookie name: discovery-browser.js bootstrap now uses `who.cookieName ?? 'dad_donor_session'` (object was expanded to satisfy Biome formatting); dad.js discoveryFixture adds `cookieName: 'dad_donor_session'` to the two authenticated donor actors only (guest untouched). Tests: test/targets.test.js (new, 2 tests), test/policy.test.js (added 1 test; existing malformed-policy coverage intact), test/adapter.test.js (added 1 cookieName test using an `adapter.sql` stub returning {stdout:''}). Verification: `npm run lint` clean; `npm test` 105 pass / 0 fail (baseline 101 + 4 new). Note for the integration fixer: there is a `benchmark-adapter.test.js` referenced in context.json verification that does not yet exist in test/ — it is expected to arrive with FEAT-002.
